title: Oratio ad Sanctorum Coetum
author: Constantinus Imperator

passages.original: Qui reliquos omnes qui ipsum aetate praecesserant sa- pientia usque adeo superavit, ut qui a gentilibus plurimum celebrantur seu sapientes, seu philosophi, sapientiae illius aemulatores exstiterint. Pythagoras certe sapientiam ejus aemulatus, modestiae causa tan- topere celebratus est, ut Plato, vir modestissimus, abstinentiam illius velut exemplum sibi ad imitan- dum proponeret. Daniel quoque, is qui futura prae- dixit, et qui summae cujusdam magnitudinis animi specimen edidit, morumque et totius vitae sanctitate excelluit, qualem et quam asperam tyranni illius qui tum in Syria dominabatur saevitiam superavit?
passages.english: He so far surpassed in wisdom all the others who had preceded him in time that those who are most celebrated among the gentiles, whether as sages or as philosophers, have shown themselves emulators of his wisdom. Pythagoras, certainly, having emulated his wisdom, was so greatly celebrated for his self-restraint that Plato, a most restrained man, set his abstinence before himself as an example to imitate. Daniel too, the one who foretold things to come, who gave proof of a certain supreme greatness of soul and excelled in holiness of character and of his whole life, what sort of savagery, and how harsh, did he overcome in that tyrant who then ruled in Syria?
passages.notes: "He" in the first sentence is Moses, the subject of the preceding context. "Syria" here stands for the realm of Nebuchadnezzar (named in the following context), i.e. Assyria/Babylon. The scanning breaks (sa- pientia, tan- topere, imitan- dum, prae- dixit) have been read as whole words.
